record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Let S be the smallest class of topological groups generated by all compact separable groups and all countable groups and closed under finite products, taking closed subgroups, and taking continuous homomorphic images. Is a topological group G in S if and only if G contains a compact separable subgroup K such that the quotient space G/K is countable?

evidence.quote: Does a topological group G belong to the class S if and only if G contains a compact separable subgroup K such that the quotient space G/K is countable?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a 2019 survey on separability of topological groups. A web search did not surface any subsequent paper claiming a resolution of this specific characterization of the class generated by compact separable groups and countable groups.
